{"id": "323f2186-6058-460a-b174-ddaeec861291", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_oZtdop31lzrZuwiM538Y8r", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Managing Skills from Chat\\\\n\\\\n## Skill Type Glossary\\\\n\\\\n| Type | Display Name | Description | Managed by |\\\\n|------|-------------|-------------|------------|\\\\n| **SYSTEM** | *(hidden)* | Built-in skills shipped with the agent (e.g. investigations, recommendations). Never visible to users. | Engineering team |\\\\n| **LEARNED** | Managed skills | Skills created by DevOps Agent. Editable and refreshed from Chat. | DevOps Agent / User (via Chat edits + refresh) |\\\\n| **USER** | Custom skills | Skills created and updated by the user through chat. Full CRUD operations supported. | User (via these tools) |\\\\n\\\\nSome managed skills can be refreshed through their dedicated tools.\\\\n\\\\n## Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\n\\\\nManaged (LEARNED) skills are migrating to memory stores: the same learned content, held as\\\\nmemories instead of a skill. The migration runs per agent space, so at any moment a given\\\\nkind may exist as a skill, as a memory store, or both during the transition.\\\\n\\\\n**When both exist for the same kind, the memory store is the home and the LEARNED skill is the\\\\nstale copy.** Read and edit the memory, not the skill, and tell the user where it now lives.\\\\n\\\\n1. When a request concerns learned understanding the DevOps Agent generates (the learned\\\\n   stores that the `manage-memories` skill\\'s glossary enumerates), check for a memory store of\\\\n   that name before reaching for `get_skill`.\\\\n2. If a memory store exists for it, load the `manage-memories` capability and work there,\\\\n   following its learned-store workflow.\\\\n3. If only the skill exists, this space has not migrated yet \\\\u2014 use the skill tools as below.\\\\n4. Do not \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a migrated skill by editing the leftover skill copy; that edit does not reach\\\\n   the agents now reading the memory.\\\\n\\\\n## Hard Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Create and delete apply only to custom (USER) skills \\\\u2014 managed (LEARNED) skills cannot be created or deleted from Chat.\\\\n- To edit a managed skill\\'s content, use `update_skill`. Do not silently substitute a custom skill that happens to share a name \\\\u2014 confirm you are editing the intended skill.\\\\n- Editing a managed (LEARNED) skill has refresh/durability considerations \\\\u2014 see \\\\\"Edit a Managed Skill\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## General\\\\n\\\\nWhen the user refers to a skill by name and you don\\'t have its knowledge_item_id, call `list_skills` to find it by name and confirm with the user before proceeding.\\\\n\\\\n## Operations\\\\n\\\\n### Create a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to create a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Check for existing skills first** \\\\u2014 call `list_skills` and review the results. If an existing skill covers a similar domain or purpose, suggest updating it instead of creating a new one. For example, if the user asks to \\\\\"create a skill for RDS troubleshooting\\\\\" and there\\'s already an \\\\\"investigate-rds-issues\\\\\" skill, propose adding the new instructions to that skill. Only proceed with creation if no existing skill is a good fit, or the user explicitly wants a new one.\\\\n2. **Gather requirements** \\\\u2014 purpose, instructions, and whether the skill needs reference files\\\\n   - A skill only needs SKILL.md if the instructions fit in one document\\\\n   - Add reference files when the skill needs: runbook templates, API reference docs, configuration examples, troubleshooting decision trees, or service-specific guides that would bloat SKILL.md\\\\n   - Organize reference files by purpose: `references/` for documentation, `assets/` for templates and config files\\\\n   - Keep SKILL.md focused on the workflow and decision logic; put detailed reference material in separate files that the agent loads on demand\\\\n2. **Generate SKILL.md** with valid YAML frontmatter and markdown body\\\\n3. **Call `create_skill`** with title, content, and optionally resources\\\\n   - `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - If the skill needs reference files: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resources={\\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Guide content\\\\\", \\\\\"references/examples.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Examples\\\\\"})`\\\\n4. **Show the user what was created** \\\\u2014 mention the skill name, description, and key steps. Do not show the ID.\\\\n5. **Ask the user to confirm** \\\\u2014 Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"Would you like me to activate this skill?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Activate\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Make this skill available for use\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Keep inactive\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Save the skill but don\\'t activate it yet\\\\\"}\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\\\\n6. **On confirmation** \\\\u2014 call `activate_skill` with the knowledge_item_id to make it live\\\\n7. **The skill is now available** \\\\u2014 `create_skill` returns the skill content in its response, so you already have the instructions. No need to call `get_skill` separately. Close the flow in prose (e.g. \\\\\"Skill is now active.\\\\\"). Do not call `ask_user` again after activation \\\\u2014 no follow-up menus.\\\\n\\\\n### Update a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to edit or update a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read current content** \\\\u2014 use `get_skill` to get the current SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Apply changes** \\\\u2014 modify the content as requested\\\\n3. **Call `update_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and updated content\\\\n   - `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - To add a resource file: `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/new.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"ADD\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# New content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To edit a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"EDIT\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# Updated content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To delete a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/old.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"DELETE\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - Multiple mutations can be combined in a single call\\\\n\\\\n### Edit a Managed Skill (LEARNED)\\\\n\\\\nManaged skills hold learned content, so a direct edit follows the **same durability rule as a learned memory store**: it is **transient** \\\\u2014 the DevOps Agent\\'s next regeneration overwrites it. Confirm this kind has not already migrated to a memory store (see \\\\\"Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\\" above for that routing) before editing here, then apply the skill-specific mechanics below and tell the user a direct edit may not persist.\\\\n\\\\nSkill-specific mechanics for the direct edit:\\\\n1. **Confirm the target** \\\\u2014 read `skillKnowledgeItemId` from the page context.\\\\n2. **Make the edit** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` for current content, then `update_skill`.\\\\n\\\\n### Delete a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to remove a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Identify the skill** \\\\u2014 use `list_skills` if needed\\\\n2. **Confirm** \\\\u2014 always ask the user to confirm before deleting\\\\n3. **Call `delete_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id\\\\n4. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm deletion\\\\n\\\\n### Read a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see a skill\\'s content, explain what a skill does, or view its files:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `get_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id to get the SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Explain** \\\\u2014 summarize the skill\\'s purpose, steps, and when it\\'s used\\\\n3. **If the skill has resource files** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` with `return_manifest=true` to see all files, then use `path` to read specific resource files\\\\n\\\\n### List Skills\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see their skills:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `list_skills`** \\\\u2014 returns agent space skills\\\\n2. **Present every skill individually** \\\\u2014 list each skill as a bullet: name \\\\u2014 description. Never group, merge, or deduplicate skills.\\\\n\\\\n### Enable or Disable a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to enable, disable, activate, or deactivate a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `toggle_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and `enabled=true` or `enabled=false`\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new status. Disabled skills remain in the agent space but are not loaded by agents\\\\n\\\\n### Change Agent Type\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to change which agent types can use a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `update_skill_agent_type`** with the knowledge_item_id and the desired agent_types list \\\\u2014 see the tool\\'s `agent_types` parameter for the accepted values\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new agent type targeting\\\\n\\\\n## SKILL.md Format\\\\n\\\\nCreate a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and markdown body:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: my-skill-name\\\\ndescription: Brief description of what this skill does. Be specific about when\\\\n  the agent should use this skill (minimum 100 characters recommended).\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Skill Title\\\\n\\\\nInstructions for the agent when this skill is activated.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- Condition 1\\\\n- Condition 2\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Step one\\\\n2. Step two\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Frontmatter Rules\\\\n- `name`: Required. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (max 64 chars). Must not start or end with a hyphen. Example: `rds-throttling-investigation`\\\\n- `description`: Required. Brief explanation of when to use this skill (min 100 chars recommended, max 1024 chars).\\\\n\\\\n### Resource Files\\\\n\\\\nSkills can include reference files alongside SKILL.md. Reference files provide additional context the agent can load on demand. Use resource files when the skill needs supporting documentation, examples, API references, or other supplementary content.\\\\n\\\\n**Allowed file types:** `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.xml`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.pdf`\\\\n\\\\n**Restrictions:**\\\\n- No script files (`.sh`, `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.rb`, `.pl`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.exe`)\\\\n- No `scripts/` directory\\\\n- No files with shebang (`#!`) content\\\\n- Maximum 100 files, 6 MB total\\\\n\\\\n## Example\\\\n\\\\nUser: \\\\\"Create a skill that helps investigate Lambda cold start issues\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n1. Generate SKILL.md:\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: investigate-lambda-cold-starts\\\\ndescription: Investigate Lambda cold start latency issues by analyzing CloudWatch\\\\n  metrics, X-Ray traces, and function configuration. Use when users report slow\\\\n  Lambda response times or CloudWatch shows elevated Init Duration metrics.\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Investigating Lambda Cold Starts\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- User reports slow Lambda response times\\\\n- CloudWatch shows elevated Duration or Init Duration metrics\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Check the function\\'s **Init Duration** metric in CloudWatch for the last 24h\\\\n2. Look at **Provisioned Concurrency** settings \\\\u2014 if not configured, cold starts are expected\\\\n3. Check the function\\'s **memory size** \\\\u2014 larger memory = faster init\\\\n4. Review X-Ray traces for init segment duration breakdown\\\\n5. Check if the function uses VPC \\\\u2014 VPC-attached Lambdas have longer cold starts\\\\n6. For detailed remediation options, read `references/remediation-guide.md`\\\\n7. Recommend: enable Provisioned Concurrency, increase memory, or use SnapStart (Java)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n2. If the skill needs reference files:\\\\n```python\\\\ncreate_skill(\\\\n    title=\\\\\"Investigate Lambda Cold Starts\\\\\",\\\\n    content=<SKILL.md above>,\\\\n    resources={\\\\n        \\\\\"references/remediation-guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Cold Start Remediation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Provisioned Concurrency\\\\\\\\n...\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\"references/metrics-reference.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Key CloudWatch Metrics\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Metric | Description |\\\\\\\\n...\\\\\"\\\\n    }\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n3. Otherwise: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"Investigate Lambda Cold Starts\\\\\", content=<SKILL.md above>)`\\\\n4. Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"I\\'ve created the skill in inactive state. Would you like me to activate it?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Activate\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Make this skill available for use\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Keep inactive\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Save the skill but don\\'t activate it yet\\\\\"}\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

A review\\\\nalso includes the stated root cause of the investigation.\\\\n\\\\n**The dimensions are configurable per agent space** \\\\u2014 a customer can edit the\\\\ngrading rubric (add, remove, or rename dimensions) via the grader\\'s `AGENTS.md`.\\\\nSo treat the dimension set as dynamic: report whatever dimensions each review\\\\nactually carries, and never assume a fixed list. The common default dimensions\\\\nare:\\\\n\\\\n- **Scope alignment** \\\\u2014 did the investigation address the actual alarm/problem?\\\\n- **Evidence grounding** \\\\u2014 are the conclusions backed by evidence?\\\\n- **Investigation completeness** \\\\u2014 can oncall act on the result?\\\\n- **Environment impact** \\\\u2014 do the deterministic signals support the verdict?\\\\n\\\\nA given agent space may have fewer, more, or differently named dimensions.\\\\n\\\\n**The rubric is editable.** The grading rubric lives in a **GRADER-scoped AGENTS.md**\\\\n(`agent_type` **GRADER**). If the user wants to change how investigations are graded \\\\u2014\\\\nadjust, add, drop, or rename dimensions, or change the HELPFUL/UNHELPFUL rule \\\\u2014 help them\\\\nedit that AGENTS.md. Express a priority as a prose rule, e.g. \\\\\"HELPFUL only if\\\\nscope_alignment passes\\\\\", rather than a numeric weight, since the Grader derives the verdict\\\\nfrom the per-dimension PASS/FAILs. To reset to the built-in defaults, delete the GRADER\\\\nAGENTS.md.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing Results of All Reviews\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-1: Summarize all reviews\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_grader_results`. Each entry is one completed review, carrying the\\\\n   reviewed investigation\\'s title (`investigationTitle`) and its `grade`. Use\\\\n   `createdAfter` / `createdBefore` for time-bounded requests (\\\\\"reviews from last\\\\n   week\\\\\"). Only reviewed investigations appear \\\\u2014 an unreviewed one has no entry.\\\\n2. Summarize the returned reviews: how many there are, the helpful vs. unhelpful\\\\n   split (`grade.quality_level`), and any recurring failing dimension across them.\\\\n3. If a `next_token` is returned and the user wants the full picture, page through\\\\n   with it before summarizing counts.\\\\n4. If no reviews come back, relay that none of their investigations have been\\\\n   reviewed yet (see the tool description) \\\\u2014 do not treat it as an error.\\\\n5. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer to open a specific review or to save the summary.\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-2: Compose a review-summary artifact\\\\n\\\\n1. Gather the data with `list_grader_results` (page through if needed).\\\\n2. Call `generate_artifact` with the collected review data and a clear instruction\\\\n   describing the deliverable \\\\u2014 e.g., a table of investigations with quality level\\\\n   and per-dimension verdicts, plus a chart of the helpful/unhelpful split. Pass\\\\n   the already-gathered data to `generate_artifact`; do not re-fetch it.\\\\n3. **Close** \\\\u2014 Point the user to the artifact and offer to drill into any review.\\\\n\\\\nFor a transient in-chat visual (not a saved report), prefer the\\\\n`render-inline-visual` skill instead of `generate_artifact`.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing a Single Review\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-3: One investigation\\'s review\\\\n\\\\n1. Identify the target investigation:\\\\n   - **Page context**: if `[now viewing: /investigation/<id>]` (or similar) is\\\\n     present, use that investigation.\\\\n   - **Conversation context**: if an investigation was just discussed, use it.\\\\n   - **Otherwise**: call `list_grader_results` and use `ask_user` to let the user\\\\n     pick which investigation\\'s review to open.\\\\n2. Call `get_grader_result` with the investigation\\'s task id.\\\\n3. Report the overall quality level and each dimension\\'s verdict with its\\\\n   justification. When a dimension failed, lead with the failing dimension and its\\\\n   reasoning.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer the full list of reviews or to open the investigation itself.\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-4: Previous / earlier reviews of one investigation\\\\n\\\\nAn investigation is usually reviewed once, but a re-review produces additional\\\\nreviews. To retrieve them:\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `get_grader_result` with the investigation\\'s task id and\\\\n   `include_history: true`. See the tool\\'s own description for the exact response\\\\n   fields (current review plus the earlier ones and a total count).\\\\n2. If there are no earlier reviews, tell the user this investigation has only been\\\\n   reviewed once. Do not treat that as an error.\\\\n   **But** if the response also has `scan_window_exhausted: true`, the history may\\\\n   be incomplete (older reviews fell outside the scanned window) \\\\u2014 say the earlier\\\\n   reviews shown may not be the full history rather than asserting there was only\\\\n   one review.\\\\n3. When the user wants a comparison, contrast the current grade against the most\\\\n   recent previous one: call out quality-level changes (e.g. UNHELPFUL \\\\u2192 HELPFUL)\\\\n   and any dimension verdict that flipped, with the reasoning for each.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer to open the investigation or list all reviews.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Shared Guidance\\\\n\\\\n## Not-Yet-Reviewed Investigations\\\\n\\\\n- When `get_grader_result` reports no review for an investigation, tell the user it\\\\n  hasn\\'t been reviewed yet \\\\u2014 do not treat this as an error, and do not invent a grade.\\\\n- **But** when the tool\\'s response indicates its scan window was exhausted (see the\\\\n  tool description), do NOT say the investigation was never reviewed. Relay the tool\\'s\\\\n  own message \\\\u2014 a review may exist but is older \\\\u2014 and offer to narrow by time or open\\\\n  the investigation directly.\\\\n- When a listed review reports it couldn\\'t be loaded, skip it in your counts and, if\\\\n  relevant, note that one review couldn\\'t be loaded rather than failing the whole\\\\n  summary.\\\\n\\\\n## Tool Errors\\\\n\\\\nIf `list_grader_results` or `get_grader_result` returns an \\\\\"Unknown tool\\\\\" result:\\\\n\\\\n- The skill\\'s tools were dropped from this session. {"id": "87202cae-7f3b-4327-9ad4-d894d50d433f", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_5QLdWu6xbCxXyeqwZPU4CH", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"## Customer Feedback Collection\\\\n\\\\nThis skill guides conversational collection of structured feedback on investigation accuracy. Feedback is stored as `feedback` knowledge items for reporting and consumption by the Learning Agent.\\\\n\\\\n### Coexistence with file_user_feedback\\\\n\\\\nThe two feedback mechanisms are separated by **intent**:\\\\n\\\\n- **Investigation feedback** (`submit_customer_feedback`) \\\\u2192 user is commenting on the accuracy or quality of an investigation\\'s root cause, mitigation, or findings.\\\\n- **Agent quality feedback** (`file_user_feedback`) \\\\u2192 user is commenting on the chat experience itself (e.g., \\\\\"that answer was unhelpful\\\\\", \\\\\"the agent is too slow\\\\\", \\\\\"I want to report a bug with the chat\\\\\").\\\\n\\\\n**Disambiguation rule:** If a user\\'s message is ambiguous (e.g., \\\\\"this is bad\\\\\", \\\\\"that was wrong\\\\\") and there is NO clear investigation context (no investigation discussed in the current conversation, no page context with an execution_id), ask the user to clarify before taking action:\\\\n\\\\n> \\\\\"Could you help me understand what you mean? Are you saying:\\\\n> - The investigation\\'s root cause or findings were wrong?\\\\n> - My response was unhelpful or incorrect?\\\\n> \\\\n> That way I can route your feedback to the right place.\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nOnly proceed with `submit_customer_feedback` when the user\\'s intent is clearly about investigation accuracy. If the user confirms they\\'re unhappy with the chat experience, use `file_user_feedback` instead.\\\\n\\\\n**When context IS clear** (investigation was just discussed, page context has execution_id, user mentions \\\\\"investigation\\\\\" or \\\\\"root cause\\\\\"), proceed directly with `submit_customer_feedback` without asking for clarification.\\\\n\\\\n**When user provides an explicit investigation ID:** Always call `get_investigation` first to verify it exists. If it returns an error or \\\\\"not found\\\\\", inform the user and offer to list recent investigations instead. Never ask for a verdict on an investigation you haven\\'t confirmed exists.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Choosing the verdict\\\\n\\\\nThe verdict reflects ROOT CAUSE accuracy, not mitigation accuracy. If the agent identified the wrong root cause but the suggested mitigation happened to work, the verdict is `INCORRECT`. Use `CORRECT` when the root cause matched the actual issue; otherwise use `INCORRECT`. The verdict is binary \\\\u2014 there is no partial option.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Direct verdict path\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `submit_customer_feedback` immediately with the appropriate verdict and the current investigation\\'s `execution_id`. No follow-up is required \\\\u2014 the verdict alone is a complete, actionable feedback item.\\\\n\\\\n   > **Note on `execution_id`:** Pass the investigation\\'s **task_id** (visible in the page context, or as the URL param when an investigation is open) as the `execution_id` argument. The tool resolves it internally to the ops1 `execution_id` used for storage \\\\u2014 the cross-surface key shared with the Operator App. Do NOT pass the chat session execution_id from the runtime context.\\\\n\\\\n2. If the verdict is `CORRECT`, acknowledge briefly and stop. Do NOT prompt for a root cause; there is nothing to correct.\\\\n3. If the verdict is `INCORRECT` and the user did not provide a root cause, fall through to the conversational path below to gather details (root cause, mitigation, etc.) \\\\u2014 but the initial submission with verdict-only is already persisted.\\\\n\\\\nThis is the simplest and most common path: the user is closing the loop on an investigation with a one-word verdict and expects you to act, not interrogate.\\\\n\\\\n### Overriding existing feedback\\\\n\\\\nBefore submitting, if the tool returns `status: \\\\\"requires_confirmation\\\\\"`, it means feedback already existed for this investigation. The response includes the `existing_verdict`. When this happens:\\\\n\\\\n- **Inform the user** a prior verdict already exists, surfacing the `existing_verdict` from the response: \\\\\"This investigation already has feedback recorded as [existing_verdict]. Do you want to change it to [new verdict]?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Wait for confirmation** before proceeding.\\\\n- If they confirm overwrite, call the tool again with `confirm_overwrite=true` and the same fields. The second call returns `status: \\\\\"updated\\\\\"`.\\\\n- **Note:** Updating replaces the entire content body. If the user only wants to change the verdict but keep the existing root_cause, you must re-include all prior fields in the second call.\\\\n\\\\nIf the user explicitly says they want to update/change their feedback (e.g., \\\\\"change my feedback\\\\\", \\\\\"actually it was correct\\\\\"), confirmation is implied \\\\u2014 proceed directly with `confirm_overwrite=true`.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Conversational feedback collection\\\\n\\\\n1. **Immediately submit** the verdict (`INCORRECT`). The verdict is saved even if the user provides no further details.\\\\n2. If the user provided the actual root cause in their message, pre-fill it and present for confirmation: \\\\\"I\\'ll record that the actual root cause was [X]. Does that capture it correctly?\\\\\"\\\\n3. Once root cause is confirmed, ask follow-up questions one at a time (do not dump all at once):\\\\n   - \\\\\"Was the suggested mitigation correct?\\\\\" (mitigation_appropriateness)\\\\n   - If the suggested mitigation was `INCORRECT`, \\\\\"What would the correct mitigation have been?\\\\\" (correct_mitigation)\\\\n   - \\\\\"Did the agent need your guidance during the investigation?\\\\\" (steering_needed)\\\\n4. After each answer, call `submit_customer_feedback` again with the same `execution_id`, including ALL previously collected fields plus the new answer. **Pass `confirm_overwrite=true` on these progressive re-calls** \\\\u2014 you are enriching feedback you yourself just submitted in step 1, so no user re-confirmation is needed (this differs from the \\\\\"Overriding existing feedback\\\\\" path above, which is for user-initiated changes to feedback from a prior conversation). The tool uses full-replace semantics \\\\u2014 omitted fields revert to their defaults.\\\\n5. If the user declines to elaborate (\\\\\"no thanks\\\\\", stops responding), that\\'s fine \\\\u2014 the verdict is already persisted.\\\\n\\\\n### Report to AWS opt-in\\\\n\\\\nIf the user wants to report the issue to AWS, present this disclaimer **verbatim**:\\\\n\\\\n> \\\\\"We will use the feedback you submit to troubleshoot and fix the issue. Do not enter personal, confidential, or sensitive information. By submitting this feedback, you agree that AWS may access and use the agent traces for troubleshooting purposes. These agent traces will not be used for model training.\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nWait for the user\\'s explicit confirmation (e.g., \\\\\"yes\\\\\", \\\\\"I agree\\\\\", \\\\\"go ahead\\\\\") before re-calling `submit_customer_feedback` with the report-to-AWS opt-in. (See the tool\\'s spec for the precondition.)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Accuracy reporting\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_customer_feedback` to retrieve stored feedback.\\\\n2. Summarize the results:\\\\n   - Total feedback count\\\\n   - Accuracy percentage (correct / total)\\\\n   - Breakdown by verdict\\\\n3. If the user asks for a detailed report or artifact, use the `create-artifact` skill with the feedback data.\\\\n\\\\nExamples:\\\\n- \\\\\"How accurate is my agent?\\\\\" \\\\u2192 summary stats\\\\n- \\\\\"Show me investigations where the agent was wrong\\\\\" \\\\u2192 filter by `verdict_filter=INCORRECT`\\\\n- \\\\\"Create a report for my manager\\\\\" \\\\u2192 generate artifact with accuracy trends\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## PII Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Do NOT include verbatim customer messages in the root_cause or correct_mitigation fields\\\\n- Summarize in your own words\\\\n- Resource names, ARNs, account IDs should not appear in feedback content\\\\n- Refer to resources generically (e.g., \\\\\"an EC2 instance\\\\\", \\\\\"a Lambda function\\\\\")\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
